drafts.title: Health and Safety Plan – Summer Fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Hazard identification, assessment, control and review
sections.body: This is a public summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club at Hagley Park on 13 February 2027, from 11:00 to 18:00, with up to 350 people expected. The organiser will use a risk assessment form to identify, assess, control, and review hazards before and during the event. Hazards considered will include food stalls with on-site cooking, two marquees (each under 100 sqm), a fenced bar tent, inflatables, and amplified sound. Controls will be documented and reviewed throughout the event. The organiser will monitor for new hazards as the event progresses and update controls as needed.

sections.heading: Health and safety responsibilities
sections.body: Health and safety responsibilities will be assigned to named staff and volunteers. The event manager will oversee the health and safety system. Each area (food stalls, bar tent, inflatables, marquees) will have a designated supervisor responsible for hazard management in their area. List of responsible persons: Event manager: [EVENT MANAGER NAME]; Food area supervisor: [FOOD SUPERVISOR NAME]; Bar tent supervisor: [BAR SUPERVISOR NAME]; Inflatables supervisor: [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME]; Marquee supervisor: [MARQUEE SUPERVISOR NAME].

sections.heading: Staff competency and supervision
sections.body: All staff and volunteers will be assigned roles based on their experience and skills. Those without prior experience will be supervised by a competent person in their area. The organiser will ensure all staff and volunteers understand their tasks and are supervised as needed.

sections.heading: Pre-event site inspection
sections.body: The organiser will conduct a full site inspection of Hagley Park before the event opens. This will include checking the setup of marquees, bar tent fencing, food stalls, inflatables, and sound equipment for safety. Any hazards identified will be controlled or removed before the public is allowed on site.

sections.heading: Accident register
sections.body: An accident register will be kept at the event manager’s station on site. All incidents, injuries, and near misses will be recorded immediately.

sections.heading: Emergency plan
sections.body: The organiser will prepare an emergency plan for the event. This will cover fire, medical emergencies, severe weather, lost children, and evacuation procedures. Emergency exits will be marked on the site plan. Staff will be briefed on their roles in an emergency. Contact details for emergency services and key staff will be kept at the event manager’s station.

sections.heading: Health and safety briefings
sections.body: A documented health and safety briefing will be held for all staff and volunteers before the event opens and before each shift change. The briefing will cover hazard controls, emergency procedures, and reporting lines. Attendance will be recorded.

sections.heading: Working with partners and suppliers
sections.body: The organiser will meet with all partners and suppliers (food stall operators, bar staff, inflatables provider, marquee supplier) before the event to review health and safety arrangements. Each supplier will be required to follow the event’s health and safety plan and report any hazards or incidents to the event manager immediately.

drafts.title: Hazard Register – Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Food Stall Operation and On-site Cooking
sections.body:
Activity: Preparing and serving food at four stalls, including on-site cooking.
Hazards: Burns, fire, hot surfaces, food contamination, slips from spills.
Persons at risk: Stall staff, volunteers, public (including children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Cooking equipment will be set up on stable surfaces away from public access. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets will be provided at each stall. Staff will be briefed on safe food handling and emergency procedures. Spill kits will be available and spills cleaned immediately. Handwashing facilities will be provided for staff.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Monitor food stall areas throughout the event and review procedures after the event.
Owner: [FOOD STALL COORDINATOR NAME]

sections.heading: Alcohol Service in Fenced Bar Tent
sections.body:
Activity: Sale and service of alcohol in a fenced bar tent.
Hazards: Intoxication, disorderly behaviour, underage drinking, slips or falls.
Persons at risk: Bar staff, security, patrons, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: The bar area will be fenced and access controlled by security. Only persons with proof of age will be served. Staff will be trained in host responsibility and will monitor for intoxication. Water will be freely available. Security will be present at all times.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Review bar operations during and after the event.
Owner: [BAR MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Marquee Setup and Use (Two Marquees, Largest Under 100 sqm)
sections.body:
Activity: Erecting and using two marquees, largest under 100 sqm.
Hazards: Trips, falls, collapse in high winds, manual handling injuries.
Persons at risk: Setup crew, volunteers, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Marquees will be installed by experienced crew following manufacturer instructions. Pegs and ropes will be clearly marked. Weather will be monitored and marquees evacuated if high winds are forecast. Only authorised staff will enter during setup and pack down.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Inspect marquees regularly during the event.
Owner: [SITE MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Inflatable Amusements
sections.body:
Activity: Use of inflatable amusements (e.g. bouncy castle).
Hazards: Falls, collisions, entrapment, deflation, wind-related movement.
Persons at risk: Children, supervising staff, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 4 = 16
Controls: Inflatables will be installed and supervised by trained operators. Maximum occupancy will be enforced. Inflatables will be anchored securely. Use will be suspended in high winds. Rules will be displayed and explained to users.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Ongoing supervision and weather monitoring.
Owner: [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME]

sections.heading: Amplified Sound
sections.body:
Activity: Use of amplified sound for announcements and music.
Hazards: Hearing damage, noise complaints, trip hazards from cables.
Persons at risk: Sound crew, performers, public (especially children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 3 = 9
Controls: Speakers will be positioned away from direct public access. Volume will be kept at safe levels. Cables will be covered or routed away from walkways. Sound checks will be conducted before the event.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Monitor sound levels and cable safety during the event.
Owner: [SOUND TECHNICIAN NAME]

sections.heading: General Public Attendance (Including Children)
sections.body:
Activity: Large crowd movement and general attendance, including children.
Hazards: Lost children, slips, trips, crowding, minor injuries.
Persons at risk: All attendees, especially children and elderly.
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 4 = 12
Controls: Clear signage and site maps will be provided. Lost child procedure will be in place and communicated to staff. First aid station will be clearly marked and staffed. Walkways will be kept clear. Staff and volunteers will be briefed on crowd management.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Review incident reports after the event.
Owner: [EVENT COORDINATOR NAME]

drafts.title: Alcohol Management Plan – Southshore Summer Festival 2027

sections.heading: Type of event
sections.body: The Southshore Summer Festival is a public outdoor festival at New Brighton beach on 20 March 2027, from 10:00 to 22:00, expecting up to 3,000 people. The event includes live music, food stalls, amusement rides, and alcohol sales. The crowd will be mixed ages, including families and children. Risks include intoxication, underage drinking, and managing a large, open site near the beach. Alcohol will be sold from designated areas using non-glass vessels. Weather and beach proximity will be considered in risk management. The event manager is [EVENT MANAGER NAME], with [DUTY MANAGER NAME] responsible for alcohol management.

sections.heading: Promoting your event
sections.body: All pre-event communications (website, social media, posters) will clearly state alcohol restrictions, age limits, and expected behaviour. Information about responsible drinking, ID requirements, and zero tolerance for intoxication will be included. Staff will be briefed to answer public queries about alcohol rules.

sections.heading: Intoxication
sections.body: All bar staff will be trained to monitor patrons for signs of intoxication. Anyone showing early signs will be refused service and offered water and food. If necessary, intoxicated patrons will be escorted to a safe area and arrangements made for their safe transport home. The duty manager will oversee these procedures.

sections.heading: Food
sections.body: Twelve food stalls will operate throughout the event, offering a range of meals and snacks. The food coordinator, [FOOD COORDINATOR NAME], will ensure food is available at all times alcohol is sold. Food options will be promoted via signage and event announcements. If food runs out, alcohol sales will stop until food is restocked.

sections.heading: Low and non-alcohol beverages
sections.body: The bar manager, [BAR MANAGER NAME], will ensure a reasonable range of low and non-alcoholic drinks are available at all times. These options will be promoted at the bar and through event signage. Stock levels will be checked regularly to prevent shortages.

sections.heading: Minors
sections.body: All patrons appearing under 25 will be required to show valid photo ID (passport, NZ driver licence, or HANZ 18+ card) before being served alcohol. Bar staff will be trained in ID checking procedures. Procedures for minors accompanied by parents or guardians will be confirmed: [CONFIRM: rule for minors accompanied by parent/guardian].

sections.heading: Signage
sections.body: The special licence and prohibited person signage will be displayed at each alcohol point of sale. The bar manager will be responsible for ensuring signage is visible and maintained throughout the event. Attach: signage plan.

sections.heading: Safe transport
sections.body: Safe transport options will be promoted via signage at exits and the bar, and through event announcements. Options include local taxi services, rideshare pick-up zones, and public transport information. A phone will be available at the information tent for patrons to arrange transport. Staff will encourage intoxicated patrons not to drive and assist with alternative arrangements.

sections.heading: Alcohol promotions on the day
sections.body: No promotions will encourage excessive drinking. There will be no discounts over 25%, no alcohol prizes, and no promotions targeting minors. All promotions will focus on responsible enjoyment and will be approved by the duty manager.

sections.heading: Staff training
sections.body: All staff, including bar, security, and volunteers, will receive a pre-event briefing covering host responsibility, licence conditions, intoxication monitoring, ID checks, and emergency procedures. Training will be documented and led by [TRAINING COORDINATOR NAME]. New staff will be briefed before starting their shift.

sections.heading: Incident and noting book
sections.body: An incident and noting book will be kept at the main bar. All refusals of service, removals, incidents involving intoxication, and any other relevant matters will be recorded by the duty manager or delegated staff. The duty manager will review entries and take action as needed. Estimated attendance: 3,000. Tickets are not sold for this event.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: A certified security firm, [SECURITY FIRM NAME], will be contracted. Security staff numbers and hours will be set to maintain a safe ratio for 3,000 attendees, with coverage from 09:30 to 22:30. The security coordinator, [SECURITY COORDINATOR NAME], will liaise with the firm and oversee performance. All security staff will be briefed before the event.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: The event will provide a relaxed, safe environment with appropriate lighting, seating, and entertainment. Drinking games and activities promoting excessive consumption are not permitted. No alcohol or vouchers will be given as prizes. Adequate toilets will be available throughout the site, with locations shown on the site plan. Attach: site plan.

sections.heading: Debriefing
sections.body: A debrief will be held after the event with all staff and contractors to review alcohol management and identify improvements. Police, Council, and Health representatives will be invited if required.

items.text: Documents who is in charge of the event and each area of responsibility
items.evidence: The overall event manager is [EVENT MANAGER NAME], responsible for the entire event operation. The person in charge of alcohol management is [ALCOHOL MANAGER NAME]. Food services are overseen by [FOOD RESPONSIBLE PERSON]. Low and non-alcoholic beverages are managed by [LOW/NON-ALCOHOL RESPONSIBLE PERSON]. items.text: Defines the type of event and its risks
items.evidence: The New Year's Day family concert is a public event at Hagley Park on 1 January 2027, from 4:00pm to 10:00pm, expecting around 800 people. The event is family-focused with children attending, features live music on a stage over 1m high, and includes the sale of alcohol. Risks include managing a mixed-age crowd, preventing intoxication, ensuring minors do not access alcohol, and maintaining a safe, relaxed environment.

items.text: Pre-event communication covers intoxication, alcohol restrictions, age limits and behaviour
items.evidence: Pre-event communication to staff and contractors will cover the event’s alcohol restrictions, intoxication prevention, age limits, and expected behaviour. The organiser will brief all staff on these points before the event.

items.text: Sets procedures to monitor patrons and prevent intoxication
items.evidence: All bar staff will monitor patrons for signs of intoxication and will refuse service to anyone showing signs. Staff will communicate with each other about any concerns and will intervene early if intoxication is suspected. Any intoxicated person will be removed from the licensed area and not served further alcohol.

items.text: Identifies a safe place for intoxicated patrons
items.evidence: A designated safe area will be set up away from the main event space where intoxicated patrons can wait or recover. This area will be monitored by trained staff who will regularly check on patrons and ensure their safety until they are able to leave or arrange transport.

items.text: Names who keeps food available while alcohol is sold
items.evidence: The organiser will assign [FOOD RESPONSIBLE PERSON] to ensure food is available at all times alcohol is sold.

items.text: Keeps a reasonable range of low and non-alcohol drinks available at all times
items.evidence: [LOW/NON-ALCOHOL RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure a reasonable range of low and non-alcoholic drinks are available at all times alcohol is sold.

items.text: Free water is readily available and promoted
items.evidence: Free water will be available at all bar areas and food stalls. Water stations will be clearly signed and staff will promote their availability to patrons.

items.text: Sets ID checks for anyone appearing under 25
items.evidence: All staff will check ID for anyone appearing under 25. Only valid forms of identification will be accepted.

items.text: Licence displayed and prohibited-person signage at each point of sale
items.evidence: The special licence and prohibited person signage will be displayed at each point of sale. [SIGNAGE RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will be responsible for ensuring signage is in place and visible to patrons.

items.text: Lists safe transport options and how they are promoted
items.evidence: Safe transport options will be promoted at the event, including local taxi and rideshare services. Information will be displayed at exits and bar areas. Staff will assist patrons in arranging transport if needed and phones will be available for this purpose.

items.text: Promotions do not encourage excessive drinking
items.evidence: No promotions will encourage excessive drinking. There will be no discounts over 25%, no alcohol prizes, and no advertising aimed at minors. Any promotions will be approved by the organiser to ensure compliance.

items.text: All staff are trained and briefed before the event
items.evidence: All staff, including bar, security, and volunteers, will receive a pre-event briefing covering host responsibility, licence conditions, intoxication prevention, ID checks, and their specific roles. Training will be documented by [TRAINING RESPONSIBLE PERSON].

items.text: Keeps an incident and noting book
items.evidence: An incident and noting book will be kept at the main bar. All refusals of service, removals, and incidents will be recorded by [INCIDENT BOOK RESPONSIBLE PERSON]. The organiser will review entries and act on any issues.

items.text: Details certified security (guideline: over 100 patrons)
items.evidence: A certified security firm will be contracted for the event. [SECURITY FIRM NAME] will provide [SECURITY STAFF NUMBER] staff from [SECURITY START TIME] to [SECURITY END TIME]. Security will monitor entrances, patrol the event, and assist with any incidents. [SECURITY LIAISON NAME] will liaise with security and ensure they are briefed before the event.

items.text: Adequate toilets throughout the event
items.evidence: Adequate toilets will be available throughout the event site.

items.text: Describes a system to identify, assess, control and review hazards before and during the event
items.evidence: The organiser will use a risk assessment form to identify, assess, control, and review hazards before and during the event. Hazards considered will include: food stalls with on-site cooking, two marquees (each under 100 sqm), a fenced bar tent, inflatables, children attending, and amplified sound. Controls will include isolating cooking areas, securing marquees, fencing the bar tent, supervising inflatables, and monitoring noise. The organiser will review hazards throughout the event and update controls as needed.

items.text: Assigns health and safety responsibilities to named staff, including volunteers
items.evidence: Health and safety responsibilities will be assigned to named staff and volunteers. The event health and safety manager will be [HEALTH AND SAFETY MANAGER NAME]. Each area (food stalls, bar tent, inflatables, marquees) will have a designated supervisor: [FOOD SUPERVISOR NAME], [BAR SUPERVISOR NAME], [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME], [MARQUEE SUPERVISOR NAME]. All staff and volunteers will be briefed on their responsibilities before the event.

items.text: Confirms staff have the knowledge and skills for their jobs, or will be supervised
items.evidence: All staff and volunteers will be checked to ensure they have the necessary knowledge and skills for their assigned roles. Where required, less experienced staff will be supervised by experienced team members. Supervisors will monitor staff performance throughout the event.

items.text: Includes a plan to inspect the venue for safety before the event
items.evidence: The organiser will conduct a full site inspection of Hagley Park before the event opens. This inspection will check for hazards such as trip risks, unsecured structures, and safe placement of inflatables and cooking equipment. Any issues found will be addressed before the public arrives.

items.text: States that an accident register is kept on site
items.evidence: An accident register will be kept on site at the event control point. All incidents, injuries, and near misses will be recorded in the register by the health and safety manager.

items.text: Includes an emergency plan designed for this event
items.evidence: The organiser will prepare an emergency plan specific to this event. This will cover fire, medical emergencies, severe weather, lost children, and evacuation procedures. Emergency exits and assembly points will be marked on the site plan. Staff will be briefed on emergency roles and contacts. First aid will be provided by [FIRST AID PROVIDER NAME]. Emergency services contact details will be available at the control point.

items.text: Describes a documented health and safety briefing for staff and volunteers before each session
items.evidence: A documented health and safety briefing will be held for all staff and volunteers before the event starts. The briefing will cover hazard controls, emergency procedures, accident reporting, and responsibilities. Attendance will be recorded. Additional briefings will be held if there are shift changes or new staff arrive.

items.text: Describes how partners and suppliers work together so the public is not endangered
items.evidence: The organiser will work with all partners and suppliers (food stall operators, bar staff, inflatable providers, marquee suppliers) to ensure their activities do not endanger the public. Each supplier will provide their own safety information and will be required to follow the event's health and safety procedures. The organiser will coordinate with suppliers before and during the event to monitor compliance.

items.text: Confirms the organiser will remove and dispose of all waste from the event location
items.evidence:
The organiser will ensure all waste generated at the event is collected, removed, and disposed of off-site after the event.
After the event, all waste will be removed from Hagley Park and taken to an appropriate disposal facility.

items.text: Explains how waste will be managed at the event
items.evidence:
Waste bins will be placed throughout the event area, including near food stalls, the bar tent, and activity zones. The organiser will check bins regularly and replace liners as needed.
The organiser will monitor bins during the event and remove all waste at the end of the event.
The organiser will check the event area for litter and spillages during and after the event, and will clean up as needed before leaving the site.

items.text: Each row describes controls that reduce the risk to a tolerable or acceptable rating
items.evidence:
Controls: Cooking areas will be separated from public with barriers. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets will be provided at each stall. All operators will be briefed on safe food handling and emergency procedures. Spills will be cleaned immediately. Only trained staff will operate cooking equipment.
Controls: Bar area will be fenced and access controlled. Only persons with valid ID will be served. Security staff will monitor the area. Water will be freely available. Staff will be briefed on host responsibility and refusal of service. Spills will be cleaned promptly.
Controls: Marquees will be professionally installed and checked before use. Guy ropes will be clearly marked. Weather will be monitored and marquees evacuated if unsafe. Occupancy will be monitored to prevent overcrowding.
Controls: Inflatables will be set up by qualified supplier. Constant supervision by trained staff. Maximum occupancy limits enforced. Soft landing mats provided. Equipment checked regularly for secure anchoring and inflation.
Controls: Volume will be kept at safe levels. Speakers positioned away from residential areas. Cables will be covered or routed safely. Sound checks before event.
Controls: Clear signage and designated entry/exit points. Staff and volunteers stationed throughout site. Lost child procedure in place. First aid station provided. Walkways kept clear.
